question: According to Constitution of India a governor can be appointed _________

options.text: for a single state at a time

solution:
The correct answer is __**for two or more states**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to Article 153 of the Constitution of India, there shall be a Governor for each state.
 
• The 7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956 facilitated the appointment of the same person as the governor for two or more states.
 
• This provision allows for administrative efficiency and the reduction of administrative costs.
 
• The President of India appoints the Governor, who holds office during the pleasure of the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 153**

 
 
• Article 153 of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Governor for each State.
 
• However, the same Article also allows the appointment of a single person as Governor for two or more states.
 
 
 
• **7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956**
 
 
• This amendment was introduced to reorganize states on a linguistic basis.
 
• It also included a provision allowing the appointment of the same person as Governor for two or more states.
 
• This was primarily for administrative convenience and to reduce costs.
 
 
 
• **Role and Functions of a Governor**
 
 
• The Governor acts as the nominal head of a state, similar to how the President functions at the central level.
 
• The Governor's duties include appointing the Chief Minister, summoning and proroguing the state legislature, and giving assent to bills passed by the state legislature.
 
• The Governor also has discretionary powers that can be exercised as per their discretion or as directed by the President.
 
 
 
• **Appointment and Tenure**
 
 
• The Governor is appointed by the President of India and holds office at the President's pleasure.
 
• The usual term of a Governor is five years, but they can be removed earlier by the President.
 
• There are no specified qualifications for the appointment of a Governor, but the person should be an Indian citizen and should have completed the age of 35 years.
